reasoning_content:
Let me think about what I've verified so far. I have strong evidence. Let me reconsider whether to attempt a full x509 auth. That would require creating a valid PKCS#7 signature with the p12 cert, which is complex and the sign-tool needs to be called via internal service URL (not exposed to host). The frontend does this in-browser. I'll note it as a limitation but not essential — the install guide's core claim is that the platform is deployed and the admin panel and cabinet are reachable with the key files, which I've verified at HTTP level.

Let me do one more meaningful check: verify the admin-api auth endpoint responds properly (e.g., /auth/me returns 401 without auth, proving the API is wired, and /test/ping works). And confirm sign-tool is healthy (it's internal on 3004, container shows healthy via Dockerfile healthcheck). Actually all containers show healthy, and each service Dockerfile has a real HTTP /test/ping healthcheck. That's strong evidence each service's HTTP server is up and responding 200.

Let me verify a couple of API behavior details to round out: admin-api /auth/me without token should return 401 (proves auth middleware active), and confirm the register API responds. This gives behavioral evidence beyond health.

Let me also confirm the frontend at 8082 is actually the admin panel (I saw title "Liquio Admin" and bundle loads 200). Good.

I think I have enough. Let me do the final API behavior check then conclude.

action.command: cd /workspace && echo "=== admin-api /auth/me without token (expect 401) ==="; curl -s -o /dev/null -w "HTTP %{http_code}\n" --max-time 10 http://localhost:8102/auth/me; echo "=== cabinet-api /test/ping ==="; curl -s --max-time 10 http://localhost:8101/test/ping; echo; echo "=== admin-api /test/ping ==="; curl -s --max-time 10 http://localhost:8102/test/ping; echo; echo "=== register /test/ping ==="; curl -s --max-time 10 http://localhost:8103/test/ping; echo; echo "=== id-api /test/ping ==="; curl -s --max-time 10 http://localhost:8100/test/ping; echo
